summary: The note argues that urban parks and gardens are fundamental economic assets, not just aesthetic or environmental amenities. It draws on a series of experts' findings from 2023-2024 covering property values, jobs, healthcare savings, tourism, business attraction, climate resilience, equitable revitalization, peripheral industries, and the value of beauty. Together these portray green spaces as active contributors to urban economic health.
one_line: Experts' 2023-2024 findings show urban parks and gardens deliver economic value through property values, jobs, health savings, tourism, business attraction and climate resilience.
key_facts: Dr. Lillian Harwood's study, released October 14th, 2023, found property near well-maintained parks and gardens rose in value by a premium of 5 to 20%, boosting city property tax revenue.

Urban planner Marcus Young (September 23, 2023) said parks create jobs for landscape designers, gardeners, conservationists and educational program coordinators, plus pop-up vendors, fitness instructors and event organizers.

Dr. Naomi Cho's report of November 9, 2023 says cities emphasizing green spaces may see lower public health expenses, since parks promote physical activity, reduce mental stress and enhance community well-being.

Tourism expert Aiden Torres (findings dated December 1, 2023) says parks like Central Park in New York and The Royal Botanic Gardens in London draw visitors, with spending spilling over to cafes and hotels.
Business development analyst Rachel Nguyen (September 15, 2023) argued companies gravitate toward greener cities for employees' quality of life, creating a cycle that attracts an educated workforce.

Environmental engineer Simon Foster, at a climate conference on January 28, 2024, said parks absorbing floodwaters and trees cooling the urban heat island effect save millions in remedial infrastructure.
Sociologist Dr. Emma Rodriguez (February 22, 2024) said parks can revitalize communities without displacement if designed with equity in mind.
Real estate agent Jamal Asfour (March 17, 2024) said parks encourage peripheral sectors such as outdoor furniture, gardening equipment and textiles for sport and outdoor attire.
Christina Zhao, an urban aesthetics expert, told city planners on April 6, 2024 that 'beauty equates to interest, and interest translates to investment.'
The note counters the belief that green spaces simply add upkeep costs, presenting them as dynamic contributors to urban economic health.
